Thoracolumbar disk extrusion

Neurologic status improved in treated dogs with preserved deep nociception, but time to regain ambulation did not differ significantly.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Neurologic status improved in treated dogs with preserved deep nociception, but time to regain ambulation did not differ significantly.

Summary of the Evidence

One unique retrospective veterinary publication is indexed for postoperative thoracolumbar disk extrusion. Bruno et al. compared dogs receiving perilesional PBM plus rehabilitation with dogs receiving rehabilitation without PBM. The report describes a neurologic signal in a defined subgroup but no statistically significant difference in time to regain ambulation. (Bruno et al. 2020)

Human and clinical evidence

No human study was identified in the exact category. The clinical evidence concerns dogs after surgery for thoracolumbar disk extrusion, and it is not directly transferable to human spinal surgery or spinal cord injury.

Animal evidence

The retrospective comparison included 24 dogs. Treated dogs with preserved deep nociception at admission were more likely to reach a neurologic-status threshold within 30 days. Kaplan–Meier analysis did not identify a significant difference in time to ambulation, although the reported mean was numerically shorter in the PBM group. Concurrent rehabilitation and nonrandomized treatment selection limit attribution.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No in-vitro or ex-vivo record is listed in this exact category. The indexed evidence is one veterinary clinical report.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The database identifies 808 nm and 905 nm near-infrared light used perilesionally, alongside physical rehabilitation. It does not provide a sufficiently complete, comparable dose and session schedule for a protocol recommendation. Findings apply to this surgical canine population and the subgroup described by the authors.

Interpretation

This single retrospective study supports further research, not a causal efficacy claim. Baseline neurologic status, rehabilitation, and treatment selection could account for some observed differences. A prospective randomized study should stratify by deep nociception and report ambulation, neurologic function, pain, and adverse events at prespecified time points.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

The exact category contains one retrospective comparative report in 24 dogs, with PBM combined with postoperative rehabilitation. The subgroup signal depended on preserved deep nociception at admission, and time to ambulation was not significantly different. Prospective controlled cohorts should test recovery outcomes separately.
